title: "os.Root: Traversal-Resistant File Access"
---

# os.Root: Traversal-Resistant File Access

## Thesis

Any code that joins a **trusted directory** with an **untrusted name** — an upload handler, an archive extractor, a static file server, a per-tenant storage layer — is one symlink away from reading or writing somewhere else. Lexical checks (`filepath.Clean`, `filepath.IsLocal`, a `HasPrefix` jail) only inspect the *string*; the kernel resolves the *filesystem*, and the two disagree the moment a symlink exists. Since Go 1.24 the standard library has the right tool: **`os.Root`**, a handle on a directory whose every operation is resolved inside that directory or refused. Go 1.25 filled in the rest of the API (`MkdirAll`, `ReadFile`, `WriteFile`, `Symlink`, `Rename`, `RemoveAll`, and friends), so on Go 1.27 there is no longer an excuse to build host paths by hand.

## Mental model

`os.OpenRoot(dir)` opens a file descriptor on `dir`. Every method on the returned `*os.Root` takes a name **relative to that descriptor** and walks it one component at a time with the `openat` family of system calls. At each step it checks: did `..` climb above the root? Did a symlink point above the root, or to an absolute path? If yes, the call fails with a `*PathError` whose message is `path escapes from parent`.

```text
classic jail                         os.Root
-------------                        -------
string  "avatar/secret.txt"          fd(work/uploads)
  |  Clean + Join + HasPrefix          |  openat(fd, "avatar")    -> symlink "../private"
  v  "work/uploads/avatar/secret.txt"  |  resolve: climbs above fd -> refuse
kernel open() follows the symlink     v
  -> work/private/secret.txt  (leak)  error: path escapes from parent
```

Three properties matter in practice:

| Property | Consequence |
|----------|-------------|
| Resolution happens **in the kernel walk**, not before it | No time-of-check/time-of-use gap between "validate" and "open" |
| Symlinks and `..` are **allowed while they stay inside** | `root.Open("a/../b")` and in-root links still work |
| The root is a **descriptor**, not a path (Linux, macOS, BSD) | Renaming or moving the directory does not redirect later operations |

The method set mirrors package `os`: `Open`, `OpenFile`, `Create`, `ReadFile`, `WriteFile`, `Mkdir`, `MkdirAll`, `Remove`, `RemoveAll`, `Rename`, `Link`, `Symlink`, `Readlink`, `Stat`, `Lstat`, `Chmod`, `Chown`, `Lchown`, `Chtimes`, plus `OpenRoot` (a narrower root inside this one) and `FS` (an `io/fs.FS` view that implements `StatFS`, `ReadFileFS`, `ReadDirFS`, and `ReadLinkFS`). For one-off opens there is `os.OpenInRoot(dir, name)`.

Rule of thumb from the Go team, and the one this chapter follows: if you are about to call `filepath.Join(fixedDir, externalName)`, use `os.Root` instead.

## Worked examples

Every listing below was run with **Go 1.27.1 on Linux (amd64)**; the output blocks are copied from those runs. Each case lives in its own directory so `go run` sees one `main` package.

### Case 1: The prefix-check jail leaks through a symlink

The classic defence cleans the name, joins it to the root, and checks the prefix. It defeats `../` — and nothing else. Here an attacker who can write into `uploads/` (a previous upload, an unpacked archive, a shared volume) plants `avatar -> ../private`.

```bash
mkdir -p case1 && cd case1
```

```go
// escape.go
package main

import (
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
)

// safeJoin is the classic lexical jail: clean, join, prefix-check.
func safeJoin(root, name string) (string, error) {
	full := filepath.Join(root, filepath.Clean("/"+name))
	if !strings.HasPrefix(full, filepath.Clean(root)+string(filepath.Separator)) {
		return "", errors.New("path escapes root")
	}
	return full, nil
}

func main() {
	// Lay out a sandbox and a secret that lives outside it.
	must(os.MkdirAll("work/uploads", 0o755))
	must(os.MkdirAll("work/private", 0o700))
	must(os.WriteFile("work/private/secret.txt", []byte("db-password=hunter2\n"), 0o600))
	must(os.WriteFile("work/uploads/hello.txt", []byte("hello\n"), 0o644))

	// Someone who can write into uploads/ plants a symlink.
	_ = os.Remove("work/uploads/avatar")
	must(os.Symlink("../private", "work/uploads/avatar"))

	for _, name := range []string{"hello.txt", "../private/secret.txt", "avatar/secret.txt"} {
		fmt.Printf("== %s\n", name)

		if p, err := safeJoin("work/uploads", name); err != nil {
			fmt.Println("  safeJoin:   rejected:", err)
		} else if b, err := os.ReadFile(p); err != nil {
			fmt.Println("  safeJoin:   error:", err)
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("  safeJoin:   read %q\n", b)
		}

		f, err := os.OpenInRoot("work/uploads", name)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Println("  OpenInRoot: rejected:", err)
			continue
		}
		b := make([]byte, 64)
		n, _ := f.Read(b)
		f.Close()
		fmt.Printf("  OpenInRoot: read %q\n", b[:n])
	}
}

func must(err error) {
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
```

```bash
go run escape.go
```

Output:

```
== hello.txt
  safeJoin:   read "hello\n"
  OpenInRoot: read "hello\n"
== ../private/secret.txt
  safeJoin:   error: open work/uploads/private/secret.txt: no such file or directory
  OpenInRoot: rejected: openat ../private/secret.txt: path escapes from parent
== avatar/secret.txt
  safeJoin:   read "db-password=hunter2\n"
  OpenInRoot: rejected: openat avatar/secret.txt: path escapes from parent
```

The string `work/uploads/avatar/secret.txt` passes every lexical test — it really is "under" `work/uploads`. The kernel follows the link anyway. `OpenInRoot` refuses both escapes and still serves the honest request. Note that `safeJoin` "handled" `../` by silently clamping it to the root, which is its own small lie: the caller asked for a file that does not exist there.

### Case 2: An archive extractor that cannot write outside its output directory

Archive extraction is the textbook traversal bug ("zip slip"): entries named `../x`, absolute names, and — the one most hand-rolled guards miss — a symlink entry followed by a file entry *through* that symlink. The extractor below never constructs a host path; every write goes through the `Root`.

```bash
mkdir -p case2 && cd case2
```

```go
// untar.go
package main

import (
	"archive/tar"
	"bytes"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"io/fs"
	"os"
)

// hostileTar builds an archive the way an attacker would.
func hostileTar() *bytes.Buffer {
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	tw := tar.NewWriter(&buf)
	add := func(h *tar.Header, body string) {
		h.Size = int64(len(body))
		if h.Mode == 0 {
			h.Mode = 0o644
		}
		if err := tw.WriteHeader(h); err != nil {
			panic(err)
		}
		io.WriteString(tw, body)
	}
	add(&tar.Header{Name: "docs/", Typeflag: tar.TypeDir, Mode: 0o755}, "")
	add(&tar.Header{Name: "docs/readme.txt", Typeflag: tar.TypeReg}, "fine\n")
	add(&tar.Header{Name: "../escape.txt", Typeflag: tar.TypeReg}, "dotdot\n")
	add(&tar.Header{Name: "/etc/evil.conf", Typeflag: tar.TypeReg}, "absolute\n")
	add(&tar.Header{Name: "link", Typeflag: tar.TypeSymlink, Linkname: "../outside"}, "")
	add(&tar.Header{Name: "link/pwned.txt", Typeflag: tar.TypeReg}, "via symlink\n")
	tw.Close()
	return &buf
}

// extract writes every entry through root. It never builds a host path.
func extract(root *os.Root, r io.Reader) error {
	tr := tar.NewReader(r)
	var errs []error
	for {
		h, err := tr.Next()
		if err == io.EOF {
			break
		}
		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, tar.ErrInsecurePath) {
			return err
		}
		if err := extractOne(root, h, tr); err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("  skip %-16s %v\n", h.Name, err)
			errs = append(errs, err)
			continue
		}
		fmt.Printf("  ok   %s\n", h.Name)
	}
	return errors.Join(errs...)
}

func extractOne(root *os.Root, h *tar.Header, body io.Reader) error {
	mode := fs.FileMode(h.Mode).Perm()
	switch h.Typeflag {
	case tar.TypeDir:
		return root.MkdirAll(h.Name, mode|0o700)
	case tar.TypeSymlink:
		return root.Symlink(h.Linkname, h.Name)
	case tar.TypeReg:
		f, err := root.OpenFile(h.Name, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_EXCL, mode)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		_, err = io.Copy(f, io.LimitReader(body, 1<<20))
		return errors.Join(err, f.Close())
	default:
		return fmt.Errorf("unsupported type %q", h.Typeflag)
	}
}

func main() {
	must(os.MkdirAll("out", 0o755))
	must(os.MkdirAll("outside", 0o755))

	root, err := os.OpenRoot("out")
	must(err)
	defer root.Close()

	fmt.Println("extracting:")
	err = extract(root, hostileTar())
	fmt.Println("errors:", err != nil)

	_, err = os.Stat("outside/pwned.txt")
	fmt.Println("outside/pwned.txt exists:", err == nil)
	_, err = os.Stat("escape.txt")
	fmt.Println("escape.txt exists:", err == nil)
}

func must(err error) {
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
```

```bash
rm -rf out outside   # O_EXCL makes reruns fail otherwise
go run untar.go
find out outside | sort
```

Output:

```
extracting:
  ok   docs/
  ok   docs/readme.txt
  skip ../escape.txt    openat ../escape.txt: path escapes from parent
  skip /etc/evil.conf   openat /etc/evil.conf: path escapes from parent
  ok   link
  skip link/pwned.txt   openat link/pwned.txt: path escapes from parent
errors: true
outside/pwned.txt exists: false
escape.txt exists: false
out
out/docs
out/docs/readme.txt
out/link
outside
```

Things worth copying from this listing:

- `O_CREATE|O_EXCL` refuses to overwrite an existing entry — including a link the archive planted earlier under the same name.
- `io.LimitReader` caps each entry; traversal is not the only hostile property of an archive.
- `archive/tar` only returns `tar.ErrInsecurePath` from `Next` when you run with `GODEBUG=tarinsecurepath=0`; the default still hands you the header. The extractor tolerates both, because the `Root` is the real guard, not the header check.
- `out/link` was created and points outside. `Root` stopped every *traversal* of it, but it did not stop its *creation*. See "The trap".

### Case 3: Serving static files — `http.Dir` versus `root.FS()`

`http.Dir` rejects `..` in URLs but follows any symlink on disk. If a deploy step, a CMS, or a user can create links under the web root, `http.Dir` will serve whatever they point at. `http.FileServerFS(root.FS())` serves the same tree with `Root` semantics.

```bash
mkdir -p case3 && cd case3
```

```go
// serve.go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	must(os.MkdirAll("site", 0o755))
	must(os.MkdirAll("private", 0o700))
	must(os.WriteFile("site/index.html", []byte("<h1>home</h1>\n"), 0o644))
	must(os.WriteFile("private/id_ed25519", []byte("-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----\n"), 0o600))
	_ = os.Remove("site/assets")
	must(os.Symlink("../private", "site/assets")) // planted by a compromised deploy step

	root, err := os.OpenRoot("site")
	must(err)
	defer root.Close()

	handlers := []struct {
		label string
		h     http.Handler
	}{
		{"http.Dir ", http.FileServer(http.Dir("site"))},
		{"root.FS()", http.FileServerFS(root.FS())},
	}
	for _, tc := range handlers {
		srv := httptest.NewServer(tc.h)
		for _, path := range []string{"/index.html", "/assets/id_ed25519"} {
			resp, err := http.Get(srv.URL + path)
			must(err)
			body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
			resp.Body.Close()
			fmt.Printf("%s %-20s %d %q\n", tc.label, path, resp.StatusCode, firstLine(body))
		}
		srv.Close()
	}
}

func firstLine(b []byte) string {
	for i, c := range b {
		if c == '\n' {
			return string(b[:i])
		}
	}
	return string(b)
}

func must(err error) {
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
```

```bash
go run serve.go
```

Output:

```
http.Dir  /index.html          200 "<h1>home</h1>"
http.Dir  /assets/id_ed25519   200 "-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----"
root.FS() /index.html          200 "<h1>home</h1>"
root.FS() /assets/id_ed25519   500 "500 Internal Server Error"
```

The escape becomes a `500`, not a `404`: the file server maps only `fs.ErrNotExist` and `fs.ErrPermission` to friendly codes, and "path escapes from parent" is neither. That is acceptable for a static site — and a useful alert signal. If you want a `404`, wrap the `fs.FS` and translate errors yourself; do not "fix" it by going back to `http.Dir`.

### Case 4: Per-tenant roots that survive a rename

A `Root` can open a narrower `Root`. Give each tenant its own and cross-tenant access becomes impossible by construction rather than by review. Because the root is a descriptor, an operator moving the data directory mid-flight does not redirect writes to whatever now sits at the old path.

```bash
mkdir -p case4 && cd case4
```

```go
// tenants.go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	must(os.MkdirAll("data/tenants/acme", 0o755))
	must(os.MkdirAll("data/tenants/globex", 0o755))

	data, err := os.OpenRoot("data")
	must(err)
	defer data.Close()

	// Narrow the jail per tenant: a Root opened from a Root.
	acme, err := data.OpenRoot("tenants/acme")
	must(err)
	defer acme.Close()
	fmt.Println("acme root name:", acme.Name())

	must(acme.WriteFile("invoice-001.json", []byte(`{"total":42}`), 0o644))
	_, err = acme.ReadFile("../globex/invoice-001.json")
	fmt.Println("cross-tenant read:", err)

	// An operator renames the data directory while the service runs.
	must(os.Rename("data", "data.old"))
	must(acme.WriteFile("invoice-002.json", []byte(`{"total":7}`), 0o644))

	entries, err := os.ReadDir("data.old/tenants/acme")
	must(err)
	for _, e := range entries {
		fmt.Println("on disk:", "data.old/tenants/acme/"+e.Name())
	}
}

func must(err error) {
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
}
```

```bash
rm -rf data data.old   # the program renames data -> data.old
go run tenants.go
```

Output:

```
acme root name: data/tenants/acme
cross-tenant read: openat ../globex/invoice-001.json: path escapes from parent
on disk: data.old/tenants/acme/invoice-001.json
on disk: data.old/tenants/acme/invoice-002.json
```

`Name()` reports the path the root was opened with; after the rename that string is stale, but the descriptor is not — `invoice-002.json` landed in the moved directory. Log `Name()` for humans; never re-open by it.

## The trap

**1. Treating `Root` as a sandbox.** `os.Root` stops *path traversal by things an ordinary user can create* — `..` and symlinks. Its documentation is explicit that it does **not** stop traversal across bind mounts or other mount points, does not block `/proc` magic files, and does not stop opening device nodes inside the root. If the threat includes a process with mount privileges, you need namespaces, a container, or a separate user — not a different file API.

**2. Letting hostile symlinks outlive the extraction.** Case 2 left `out/link -> ../outside` on disk. Your `Root` will never follow it, but the next program that runs `cp -r out/ …` or a plain `os.Open` will. Validate link targets *before* creating them:

```go
// linkcheck.go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"path/filepath"
)

// localLink reports whether a symlink named name with target target
// would stay inside the extraction root when followed.
func localLink(name, target string) bool {
	if filepath.IsAbs(target) {
		return false
	}
	return filepath.IsLocal(filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(name), target))
}

func main() {
	for _, l := range [][2]string{
		{"link", "../outside"},
		{"docs/latest", "v2"},
		{"docs/up", ".."},
		{"docs/abs", "/etc"},
		{"a/b/c", "../../d"},
	} {
		fmt.Printf("%-12s -> %-11s local=%v\n", l[0], l[1], localLink(l[0], l[1]))
	}
}
```

```bash
go run linkcheck.go
```

Output:

```
link         -> ../outside  local=false
docs/latest  -> v2          local=true
docs/up      -> ..          local=true
docs/abs     -> /etc        local=false
a/b/c        -> ../../d     local=true
```

The lexical check is fine *here* because it runs on archive metadata, not on the live filesystem, and `Root` still guards the actual writes. Belt and braces: `Root` for every operation, `IsLocal` for what you agree to leave behind.

**3. Matching the error string.** The "escapes" error is an unexported sentinel wrapped in `*os.PathError`; there is no `errors.Is` target for it. Treat **any** error from a `Root` method on untrusted input as a rejection. Do not string-match `"path escapes"` to decide whether to retry somewhere else.

**4. Using `Root` where the user owns the path.** A CLI flag like `-o /tmp/report.csv` is a *trusted* path chosen by the operator. Jailing it inside the working directory is a bug, not hardening. `Root` is for names that arrive from outside the trust boundary.

**5. Assuming every method is race-free.** On Unix, `Root.Chmod`, `Root.Chown`, and `Root.Chtimes` can act on a symlink if the target is swapped between check and use (documented limitation). Do metadata changes on a file you just opened, or on entries you created yourself in the same operation.

**6. Forgetting the cost.** Resolving component-by-component is more expensive than one `open(2)`, and many `..` segments make it worse. Reject absurd names early (length, depth, `filepath.IsLocal`) — for cost and clarity, not for safety; safety comes from the `Root`.

## The boring rule

> Open the trusted directory **once** with `os.OpenRoot`, keep the `*os.Root` for the life of the component, and route **every** operation on an untrusted name through it — never `filepath.Join` a fixed directory with external input, never re-open by `Root.Name()`, and treat every `Root` error as "no".

## Try this

1. In Case 1, replace the symlink with a hard link (`os.Link("../private/secret.txt", "work/uploads/avatar.txt")`). Run it. Explain why `Root` allows the read (hint: a hard link is a second *name* for the same inode, not a path that points elsewhere — `Root` guards name resolution, and Linux's `fs.protected_hardlinks` is what limits who may create such links).
2. Extend Case 2 to call `localLink` before `root.Symlink` and skip escaping links. Confirm `out/link` no longer exists after extraction.
3. Rerun Case 2 with `GODEBUG=tarinsecurepath=0 go run untar.go` and add a log line when `Next` returns `tar.ErrInsecurePath`. Which entries does the header check catch, and which one (hint: the symlink pair) does only `Root` catch?
4. Wrap `root.FS()` in Case 3 with your own `fs.FS` whose `Open` converts any non-`ErrNotExist` error into `fs.ErrNotExist`, so escapes return `404`. Log the original error.
5. In Case 4, start a goroutine that writes to `acme` in a loop while `main` renames `data` back and forth. Run with `-race`. `Root` methods are documented safe for concurrent use; verify the race detector agrees.
6. Grep your own services for `filepath.Join(` followed by a request field, form value, or archive header name. Convert one to `os.Root` and keep its old test cases passing.
